title: Counterfactual Explainability and Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Inspection for Reliable Steel Surface Defect Recognition
content: Reliable steel surface defect recognition is important for industrial quality control, where inaccurate classification and limited model interpretability can affect inspection decisions. This study presents a simulation-based computational experimental investigation of deep learning-based steel defect recognition through a framework integrating counterfactual explainability, predictive uncertainty, explanation stability, and adaptive inspection. Computational experiments were conducted using the NEU-DET dataset, which contains six steel surface defect categories. Four deep learning architectures, namely ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, MobileNetV3Large, and AttentionCNN, were evaluated across five independent random seeds. Classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, macro F1-score, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC. Computational efficiency was evaluated through training time, inference latency, throughput, parameter count, and model size. ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNetV3Large achieved 100% validation accuracy and macro F1-score across the recorded runs. AttentionCNN achieved 77.67% validation accuracy and 76.66% macro F1-score, with the lowest inference latency of 1.50 ms and a model size of 1.71 MB. Additional computational simulations were designed to examine classification robustness under controlled image perturbations, counterfactual explanation quality, predictive uncertainty, explanation stability, and adaptive inspection decisions. The results provide a comparative assessment of classification performance and computational efficiency while presenting a unified computational framework for examining prediction reliability and selective inspection. The study is limited to dataset-based computational experiments, and its findings do not establish physical factory-level inspection performance. Further independent evaluation using additional datasets and verified inspection outcomes is required before industrial deployment.
